When the generated client lags behind the canonical schema, it introduces undefined symbols that break downstream typechecking. Codex resolves this by forcing a regeneration step, which acts as a synchronization barrier. This ensures that the abstract data model (schema) and its concrete representation (client API) are aligned, thereby preventing dynamic type errors at runtime. The safety of this fix relies on the fact that the Prisma CLI is idempotent when given a stable input schema, guaranteeing eventual consistency.
